entities.summary:
Eufrasia Burlamacchi (1482–1548) was an Italian nun who practiced the art of manuscript illumination.

Born in the Renaissance humanist city of Florence, Italy, Burlamacchi was trained in the arts by the prominent artist and illuminator, Fra Bartolomeo Savoldo.

Her most celebrated work, the 1528–1530 'Codex Aureus', is a masterpiece of Italian Renaissance manuscript illumination, featuring intricate gold leaf and fine calligraphy.

Burlamacchi's legacy extends beyond her artistic achievements, as she helped establish the nun's order of 'Sisters of the Pen', which provided education and artistic training to women from poor families.

In the years following her death in 1548, Burlamacchi's manuscripts were sold to the Holy Roman Emperor, Charles V, who used them to enrich his personal library.

The delicate, hand-painted pages of her illuminated manuscripts continue to inspire artists and historians, serving as a testament to the enduring power of her craft.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Eufrasia Burlamacchi's illuminated manuscripts, such as the 'Codex Aureus', have had a lasting impact on the development of Renaissance art, while her establishment of the 'Sisters of the Pen' order provided education and artistic training to women from poor families. Her legacy continues to inspire artists and historians, serving as a testament to the enduring power of her craft.
